terms.text: The first person in the room with the customer: a hybrid who understands engineering practice, can face the customer, and bridges their needs into working systems. Not purely an engineer.
Teaching the workflow until a team can run it: training, coaching, and sharing what works. Same practice as the build, at a different depth.
The written frame the work runs on. In a build it is the spec, the decisions, and the rules an agent can check itself against. In the practice it is the red thread through the career.
Agents that draft and check work against a frame a person owns. The person reviews the diffs and owns the outcome.
What the work creates: new products, better decisions, more stable platforms, new business. Time saved is a first measure, not the value.
The name of the practice: build, advise, and teach software with coding agents as part of the work.
The work across a software product’s lifecycle, from the need through build and test to owning the outcome. Not a single stack, and not a list of jobs in order.
One step on the maturity spiral. A turn means overcoming the bottleneck, putting the next guardrails in place, and reaching the unlock.
Teaching the new workflow through enablement and speaking. The same loop used in production, with a person in the room.
A talk or a practitioner session built from learning outcomes, on the team’s own work. A human gate stays on what ships.
Written instructions an agent can run inside the factory: curriculum, storyboard, script, slides, video, quality review. Separate from the human skills a team still has to grow.
